post.caption: Napoleon's sword once held this diamond. The Regent is named for a regent of France who once owned it. It was reportedly found at Golconda, India, around 1698, and the rough stone weighed more than 400 carats. Thomas Pitt, governor of Madras, bought it around 1701, and cutting it in London took about two years. The finished cushion cut stone weighs about 140 carats. In 1717 Pitt sold it to Philippe, Duke of Orléans. In 1722 it was set in Louis XV's coronation crown, and it sat on Napoleon's sword at his 1804 coronation. The Regent has been in the Louvre's collection since 1887.
